title: Model parameter toggle and rollback runbook (safe production toggles)
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Summary:

This runbook describes the approved, low-risk procedures for toggling model-serving parameters in production and the fast rollback sequence if user-facing or billing-impacting regressions are detected. It is intended for oncall Customer Success Engineers (CSE), Site Reliability Engineers (SRE), and designated customer technical contacts during enterprise cutovers, feature flags, or emergency mitigations.

Goals and scope:

- Goal: Allow controlled, auditable changes to serving-level parameters (e.g., sampling temperature, max_tokens limit overrides, prefix caching enable/disable, quantization tier selection) while minimizing downtime and exposure.
- Scope: Applies to hosted and dedicated deployments owned by Redwood Inference where feature toggles or parameter overrides are permitted under contract. It does NOT replace scheduled model upgrades; see the model-change approval runbook for major version rollouts.

Prerequisites and access:

- Owner: Customer Success (primary), Eng-SRE (secondary).
- Required permissions: access to Redwood Console toggles UI and CLI (redwoodctl), tenant-scoped observability dashboards, and ability to create temporary routing policies.
- Pre-flight checklist (must be completed before any toggle):
  1. Confirm change approval exists (ticket or signed customer change request).
  2. Notify stakeholders via Slack #cust-x-oncall and email distribution list at least 30 minutes before a planned toggle unless it is an emergency.
  3. Ensure a canary group is available for target tenant(s) or a <1% traffic slice for platform-wide toggles.
  4. Snapshot key telemetry dashboards and export spike baselines (latency, error rate, token cost per request, top-10 request fingerprints).
  5. Confirm fallback model/quantization image artifacts are available and tested in staging.

Key SLOs and guardrails (hard thresholds):

- Latency P95 increase > 40% relative to baseline for 5 continuous minutes -> trigger rollback.
- Customer error rate (5xx or model-response-format-failures) increase > 2 percentage points absolute -> trigger rollback.
- Cost per 1k tokens increase > 30% for a sustained 10-minute window -> investigate and consider rollback.
- Significant semantic degradation (customer-reported quality drop backed by eval probes) -> immediate rollback.

Toggle categories and examples:

- Lightweight runtime flag: enable/disable KV prefix caching for a tenant. Low-risk if canaried.
- Inference parameter change: sampling temperature or repetition penalty. Medium-risk if wide rollout.
- Execution profile switch: enable fast-quantized path (e.g., 8-bit) on a model. Higher-risk; always canary and verify correctness.
- Model variant fallback: route traffic from model-v2 to model-v1. High-risk for regressions; use canary first.

Step-by-step toggle procedure (planned change):

1. Pre-checks (10–30 minutes prior):
   - Verify ticket and approvals.
   - Take telemetry snapshots: store timestamped baseline.
   - Create an incident channel and document runbook steps in the channel.
2. Canary stage (5–15 minutes):
   - Apply toggle to canary: use redwoodctl toggle set --tenant <tenant-id> --feature <flag> --value <on|off> --scope canary --pct 1
   - Observe metrics in real-time: latency, error rate, request success ratio, cost per token, and sampling entropy drift.
   - Run synthetic probe suite (3–5 queries) saved in customer-specific eval set.
3. Expand stage (15–60 minutes):
   - If canary metrics stable, incrementally increase traffic: 5% -> 20% -> 100% for the affected route over at least 15 minutes per step.
   - At each step, verify automated regression checks.
4. Full rollout and verification (30–60 minutes):
   - After reaching 100% for the target scope, continue monitoring for an additional 60 minutes and run full eval prompt set.

Emergency rollback procedure (immediate):

1. Trigger criteria: any of the Key SLO guardrails breached or a direct customer complaint indicating major regression.
2. First action (0–2 minutes):
   - Execute rollback command: redwoodctl toggle rollback --feature <flag> --target <scope> or re-route traffic: redwoodctl route set --from <model-v2> --to <model-v1> --immediate true
   - If rollback command is unavailable, set tenant to safe-mode profile: redwoodctl tenant set-profile --tenant <tenant-id> safe-mode
3. Notify stakeholders: post one-line incident summary to the incident channel and escalate to Eng-SRE via paging policy.
4. Post-rollback checks (5–15 minutes):
   - Confirm latency and error metrics returned to baseline within guardrails.
   - Re-run synthetic probes and confirm outputs match pre-toggle snapshots where applicable.
5. If rollback fails to restore baseline, escalate to SRE L2 and open a Sev ticket.

Verification queries and telemetry probes (examples):

- Query 1: P95 latency (model-route) over last 5 minutes vs baseline (stored timestamp).
- Query 2: 5xx error count and ratio by tenant per minute.
- Query 3: Tokens billed per request aggregated by route.
- Probe harness: run 10 canonical prompts in the eval set and assert BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity thresholds (configured per customer).

Communication templates (use in incident channel and customer-facing notices):

- Slack incident message (internal):
  "[INCIDENT] Toggle <flag> for <tenant-id> applied at <ts>. Canary -> observed P95 +12%. Monitoring. If exceeds +40% rollback. Aisha oncall."

- Customer-facing brief (email/snippet):

  Subject: "Planned parameter change — status update"

  Body: "We applied a limited parameter change to <model-route> at <ts> to improve [latency/cost]. We are monitoring performance and will provide an update within 60 minutes. If you notice degraded responses, contact us at <support@redwood.ai> and we will revert immediately."

Post-change retrospective and required artifacts (within 48 hours):

- Owner creates a short post-run report documenting: change rationale, telemetry before/after (include baseline snapshots), probe results, and any customer impact. Attach toggling command history and audit logs.
- If rollback occurred, file a postmortem if impact reached Severity 2 or higher (see incident-process/playbooks).

Automation and tooling recommendations:

- Always use redwoodctl for toggles in scripted contexts to preserve audit logs.
- Ensure the Synthetic Probe Runner job is available for the tenant and quarantined to only use non-sensitive prompts.
- Add automated checks in the deployment pipeline to halt expansion on threshold breaches.

Ownership and escalation matrix:

- Primary: Customer Success (CSE) named contact for tenant.
- Secondary: Eng-SRE oncall (pager duty).
- Tertiary: Runtime Engineering (for kernel/quantization path issues) and Applied ML team (for semantic regressions).

Appendix: CLI examples and safe-mode presets:

- Toggle example (canary):
  redwoodctl toggle set --tenant tenant-1234 --feature kv-cache --value enabled --scope canary --pct 1

- Full rollback example (route):
  redwoodctl route set --from model-v2 --to model-v1 --immediate true --reason "rollback due to P95 spike"

- Safe-mode profile JSON (apply with redwoodctl profile apply --tenant):
  {
    "name": "safe-mode",
    "max_tokens": 512,
    "temperature": 0.0,
    "enable_kv_cache": false,
    "quantization_profile": "stable-8bit"
  }
